definition: A casual greeting used any time of day.
examples: I walked in and said {hallo} to everyone.
sentences: {Hello}! Is this seat taken?
{Hello}, I love your café!

definition: A polite morning greeting, used until about noon.
examples: She greeted the baker with a cheerful {guten Morgen}.
sentences: {Good morning}! Is the coffee ready?
{Good morning}! What a lovely garden you have.

definition: A formal evening greeting, used from late afternoon onward.
examples: He tipped his hat and said {guten Abend}.
sentences: {Good evening}! Are you still open?
{Good evening}, I'd love a table by the window.

definition: A polite way to say goodbye, literally 'until we see again'.
examples: It was nice meeting you — {auf Wiedersehen}!
She waved and said {auf Wiedersehen} as the train left.
sentences: {Goodbye}! I'll come back tomorrow.
Thanks for the coffee, {goodbye}!

definition: The standard way to express gratitude.
examples: He handed me the coffee and I said {danke}.
sentences: {Thank you} for the lovely coffee!
{Thank you}, this cake is amazing!

definition: Used to say 'please' or 'you're welcome'. Very versatile!
sentences: One espresso, {please}!
Could I sit on the patio, {please}?

definition: The word for 'yes'. Short, simple, essential.
examples: {Ja}, I think that's a great idea.
sentences: {Yes}, I'd love another cup!
{Yes}, this is my favorite café!

definition: The word for 'no'. Firm and clear.
examples: {Nein}, I don't want any more sugar.
She shook her head and said {nein}.
sentences: {No}, no sugar for me today.
{No} thanks, I'm just reading my book.

definition: Borrowed from English — means the same thing!
sentences: {Okay}, I'll try the house special!
Is it {okay} if I sit in the garden?

definition: Used to apologize or get someone's attention politely.
examples: {Entschuldigung}, I didn't mean to bump into you.
sentences: {Excuse me}, is this the reading room?
{Excuse me}, could I see the menu?

definition: A warm way to say 'you're welcome' or 'here you go'.
sentences: {You're welcome}! Enjoy your coffee.
{You're welcome}, come back anytime!

definition: Literally 'it does me sorrow'. A heartfelt apology.
examples: {Tut mir leid}, I broke your favorite cup.
Oh no, {tut mir leid} — I forgot your birthday!
sentences: {Sorry}, I spilled coffee on the table!
{Sorry}, is this chair taken?

definition: The number one. The starting point of counting.
sentences: Just {one} coffee for me, thanks!
I've been waiting for {one} hour already.

definition: The number two.
examples: We waited {zwei} hours for the bus.
sentences: Can I get {two} cups of tea?
There are {two} empty seats on the patio!

definition: The number three.
examples: There are {drei} cats in the garden.
Give me {drei} minutes and I'll be ready.
sentences: I come here at least {three} times a week.
Table for {three}, please!

definition: The number four.
examples: We need {vier} tickets for the movie.
sentences: We need {four} chairs at this table.
I've tried {four} different cakes here!

definition: The number five. High five!
examples: I have {fuenf} fingers on each hand.
sentences: I'll be there in {five} minutes!
This café has {five} stars in my book.

definition: The number six.
examples: There are {sechs} eggs in the box.
sentences: I've been reading here for {six} hours!
There are {six} plants on that shelf.

definition: The number seven. A lucky number in many cultures.
examples: There are {sieben} days in a week.
sentences: I drink about {seven} coffees a week.
The garden has {seven} different flowers!

definition: The number eight.
sentences: Do you close at {eight}?
I've read {eight} chapters of my book today.

definition: The number nine.
examples: A cat has {neun} lives, they say.
sentences: I've been coming here since {nine} this morning!
The café opens at {nine}, right?

definition: The number ten. A perfect score!
examples: Count to {zehn} and then come find me.
I give this cake a {zehn} out of ten.
sentences: I'd give this coffee a {ten} out of ten!
There are {ten} books on the reading shelf.

definition: The color red — like roses or strawberries.
examples: She wore a {rot} dress to the party.
sentences: I love that {red} mug on the shelf!
The {red} roses in the garden are gorgeous.

definition: The color blue — like the sky or the ocean.
sentences: Can I get the {blue} cup instead?
The {blue} sky looks perfect from the patio!

definition: The color green — like grass and leaves.
examples: I love the {gruen} forest in spring.
sentences: The {green} plants make this café so cozy.
I love how {green} the garden is!

definition: The color yellow — bright like sunshine.
examples: The sunflowers are so {gelb} and cheerful.
sentences: Those {yellow} flowers in the garden are lovely!
I'll take the {yellow} teapot one.

definition: The color white — pure and clean.
examples: He wore a {weiss} shirt to work.
sentences: The {white} marble counter looks so elegant.
Can I have {white} chocolate cake?

definition: The color black. Also used in 'Schwarzwald' (Black Forest).
examples: I take my coffee {schwarz}, no milk.
sentences: I take my coffee {black}, no milk!
Is that a {black} cat in the garden?

definition: The color pink — soft and rosy.
examples: The cherry blossoms are {rosa} in spring.
sentences: The {pink} flowers on the patio are so cute!
I love the {pink} cups you have here.

definition: The color orange — same word as in English!
examples: I like {orange} juice in the morning.
sentences: Can I get an {orange} juice?
The {orange} sunset looks amazing from here!

definition: Water. 'Das' marks it as a neuter noun.
examples: Can I have a glass of {Wasser}, please?
The {Wasser} in this lake is crystal clear.
sentences: Could I get a glass of {water}?
The fountain {water} sounds so relaxing.

definition: Coffee — Germany's favorite hot drink!
examples: I can't start my day without {Kaffee}.
sentences: I can't start my day without {coffee}!
Your {coffee} is the best in town.

definition: Tea. Popular throughout German-speaking countries.
examples: I drink {Tee} when I'm feeling sick.
sentences: Could I have a cup of {tea} instead?
What kinds of {tea} do you have?

definition: Milk. A feminine noun in German.
examples: I put {Milch} in my coffee every morning.
We're out of {Milch}, can you buy some?
sentences: Can I have some {milk} in my coffee?
Do you have oat {milk}?

definition: Bread — Germany has over 3,000 types of bread!
examples: Fresh {Brot} from the bakery smells amazing.
I had {Brot} with butter for breakfast.
sentences: Do you serve fresh {bread} here?
The {bread} smells amazing!

definition: Cheese. Germany produces many varieties.
sentences: Is there {cheese} on that sandwich?
I'd love some {cheese} with my bread.

definition: Apple. The plural 'Äpfel' changes the vowel!
sentences: Do you have {apple} cake today?
I brought an {apple} from the garden.

definition: Cake. Germans love their 'Kaffee und Kuchen' tradition!
examples: Grandma's {Kuchen} is the best in town.
Let's have some {Kuchen} with our afternoon coffee.
sentences: What kind of {cake} do you have today?
This {cake} is absolutely delicious!

definition: Sugar — sweet stuff for your coffee.
sentences: Could I have some {sugar} for my tea?
No {sugar} for me, thanks!

definition: Butter — same word, different pronunciation!
sentences: Can I get some {butter} for my bread?
This cake has real {butter} in it, right?

definition: Cat. A feminine noun, because of course cats are elegant.
examples: My {Katze} loves to sleep on the sofa.
sentences: Is that your {cat} sleeping on the chair?
I saw a {cat} in the garden earlier!

definition: Dog — man's best friend in any language.
examples: I walk my {Hund} every morning in the park.
sentences: Can I bring my {dog} to this café?
My {dog} is waiting outside by the garden.

definition: Bird. Also used in the fun expression 'einen Vogel haben' (to be crazy).
examples: A {Vogel} is singing outside my window.
Look at that colorful {Vogel} in the tree!
sentences: Do you hear that {bird} singing outside?
A {bird} just landed on the patio railing!

definition: Fish — whether swimming or on your plate.
examples: There's a big {Fisch} in the pond!
sentences: Is there a {fish} in the garden pond?
I think I saw a {fish} jump!

definition: Horse. A neuter noun in German.
examples: She loves riding her {Pferd} on weekends.
sentences: I rode a {horse} before coming here!
My daughter loves drawing a {horse} in her sketchbook.

definition: House or home. 'Zu Hause' means 'at home'.
examples: The {Haus} on the corner has a beautiful garden.
sentences: My {house} is just around the corner from here.
The {house} next door has a beautiful garden too!

definition: School. Education is taken very seriously in Germany.
examples: The kids walk to {Schule} every day.
sentences: I always stop here after {school}.
My kid's {school} is right down the street.

definition: A store or shop. Can also mean 'business'.
examples: I'm going to the {Geschaeft} to buy groceries.
sentences: I just came from the {store} next door.
Is there a {store} nearby?

definition: Street or road. You'll see this in every German address.
examples: The café is on the next {Strasse}.
sentences: Which {street} is this café on?
This {street} has the best shops!

definition: Park — same word, different article!
sentences: I walked through the {park} to get here.
The {park} across the street is lovely.

definition: Mother. One of the first words many children learn.
examples: I called my {Mutter} to wish her happy birthday.
sentences: My {mother} loves this café!
I'm buying cake for my {mother}.

definition: Father. Compare with English 'father' — same roots!
examples: My {Vater} taught me to ride a bike.
sentences: My {father} always orders black coffee.
I'm meeting my {father} here for lunch.

definition: Brother. Very similar to English — both come from the same ancient root.
examples: My {Bruder} and I look nothing alike.
sentences: My {brother} is sitting over on the patio.
I'm saving this seat for my {brother}.

definition: Sister. Also means 'nurse' in a medical context!
examples: She's the best {Schwester} anyone could ask for.
sentences: My {sister} recommended this place!
I'm waiting for my {sister} — she's always late.

definition: Child. The plural 'Kinder' might remind you of a certain chocolate brand!
examples: The {Kind} is playing in the garden.
sentences: My {child} loves the garden here.
Is there a menu for a {child}?

definition: Friend. Can also mean 'boyfriend' depending on context!
sentences: I'm meeting a {friend} here for coffee.
A {friend} told me about this place!

definition: Good. As in 'alles gut' (all good).
sentences: This coffee is really {good}!
What a {good} spot to read a book.

definition: Bad. The opposite of 'gut'.
sentences: The weather outside is so {bad} today!
I hope the coffee isn't {bad} here.

definition: Big or tall. Not the English kind of 'gross'!
examples: My {Bruder} is very {gross} — almost two meters!
sentences: What a {big} garden you have!
Can I get a {big} cup of coffee?

definition: Small or little. The opposite of 'gross'.
examples: Just a {klein} piece of cake for me.
sentences: Just a {small} piece of cake for me.
This is such a cozy {small} café!

definition: Hot — for temperature or spicy food.
sentences: Careful, the coffee is really {hot}!
It's too {hot} to sit outside today.

definition: Cold. German winters are definitely {kalt}!
examples: It's so {kalt} today, I need a jacket.
Do you want {kalt} or warm water?
sentences: It's so {cold} outside — I need hot tea!
Can I get a {cold} drink instead?

definition: New. Sounds like English 'new' — they're related!
examples: Is this café {neu}? I've never seen it before.
sentences: Is this a {new} café? I love it!
Have you tried the {new} cake they have?

definition: Old — for things or people.
examples: This building is very {alt} — over 500 years!
sentences: This building looks really {old} and charming.
I love {old} cafés like this one.

definition: Beautiful, nice, or lovely. A very common compliment.
sentences: Your garden is so {beautiful}!
What a {beautiful} day to sit on the patio!

definition: Pretty or cute. More casual than 'schoen'.
sentences: What a {pretty} little café this is!
The flowers on the table are so {pretty}.

definition: To eat. Also a city name — Essen, Germany!
sentences: I'd love to {eat} some cake here!
Is there somewhere to {eat} on the patio?

definition: To drink. Think of the English word 'drink' — same roots!
examples: I like to {trinken} {Kaffee} in the morning.
sentences: I love to {drink} coffee in the garden!
What would you recommend to {drink}?

definition: To go or to walk. One of the most used verbs.
sentences: I need to {go} soon — save my seat!
Should we {go} sit in the garden?

definition: To come. 'Woher kommen Sie?' means 'Where do you come from?'
sentences: I {come} here every morning!
You should {come} try the cake!

definition: To see. 'Auf Wiedersehen' literally uses this verb!
examples: I can {sehen} the mountains from here.
sentences: Can you {see} the garden from here?
I can {see} a bird in that tree!

definition: To do or to make. Extremely versatile verb.
examples: What are you going to {machen} today?
sentences: What are you going to {do} after coffee?
I don't know what to {do} — everything looks delicious!

definition: To say or to tell.
sentences: I have to {say}, this is the best café!
I just wanted to {say} the cake was amazing.

definition: To know (a fact). Different from 'kennen' (to know a person).
sentences: Do you {know} what's on the menu today?
I didn't {know} this café had a garden!

definition: To be able to, can. A modal verb — changes sentence structure.
examples: Can you {sprechen} German? — I {koennen} a little!
sentences: Would I {be able} to sit by the window?
I'm not sure I'll {be able} to finish this huge cake!

definition: To want. Another important modal verb.
sentences: I {want} to try your famous coffee!
Do you {want} to sit inside or outside?

definition: To love or to like very much. 'Ich liebe dich' = I love you.
sentences: I really {like} this reading room!
I {like} the music playing in here.

definition: To speak. 'Sprechen Sie Deutsch?' is a classic phrase.
examples: I'm learning to {sprechen} a new language.
sentences: Do you {speak} German?
I'm trying to {speak} a little German here!

definition: To sleep. 'Gute Nacht' and then {schlafen}!
examples: I need to {schlafen} — it's been a long {Tag}.
sentences: I couldn't {sleep} last night — I need coffee!
That cat looks like it wants to {sleep} on the bench.

definition: To read. A great skill for learning German!
examples: I like to {lesen} a {Buch} before bed.
What are you reading? — I'm trying to {lesen} in German!
sentences: I love to {read} in the reading room!
Is this a good spot to {read} quietly?

definition: The sun. Feminine in German — she shines!
examples: The {Sonne} is shining so bright today.
I love sitting in the {Sonne} with my {Kaffee}.
sentences: The {sun} feels so nice on the patio!
I love having coffee in the {sun}.

definition: Rain. Germany gets plenty of it!
examples: Don't forget your umbrella — there's {Regen} coming.
I love the sound of {Regen} on the roof.
sentences: I came inside because of the {rain}.
I love listening to the {rain} from in here!

definition: Snow. Makes everything look {weiss}!
examples: The kids are playing in the {Schnee}!
sentences: Look at the {snow} in the garden!
Hot coffee is perfect when there's {snow} outside.

definition: Wind — same word as English, different pronunciation.
examples: A cold {Wind} is coming from the north.
sentences: The {wind} almost blew my napkin away!
It's too much {wind} for the patio today.

definition: Day. 'Guten Tag' is a general daytime greeting.
sentences: What a lovely {day} to sit outside!
I've had the best {day} — starting with your coffee!

definition: Night. 'Gute Nacht' means good night.
examples: The stars are {schoen} tonight — what a {Nacht}!
sentences: I was up all {night} reading my book!
Good {night}! See you tomorrow.

definition: Morning (as a noun). Don't confuse with 'morgen' (tomorrow)!
examples: I love the quiet {Morgen} with my {Kaffee}.
sentences: I come here every {morning} for coffee.
This {morning} is perfect for the garden!

definition: Evening. The time for 'Abendbrot' (evening bread/dinner).
examples: What a lovely {Abend} — the sunset is {schoen}.
sentences: The café looks so cozy in the {evening}!
I love reading here in the {evening}.

definition: Today. Very useful for making plans!
sentences: What cake do you recommend {today}?
I need extra coffee {today}!

definition: Tomorrow (lowercase). Same spelling as 'der Morgen' (morning)!
sentences: I'll come back {tomorrow} for more cake!
See you {tomorrow}!

definition: Head. 'Kopfschmerzen' means headache.
examples: Use your {Kopf} and think about it.
sentences: My {head} hurts — I need some tea.
I can't get that song out of my {head}!

definition: Hand — almost identical to English!
examples: Give me your {Hand}, I'll help you up.
She waved her {Hand} to say goodbye.
sentences: I burned my {hand} on the hot cup!
Can you give me a {hand} with these books?

definition: Heart — both the organ and the symbol of love.
examples: My {Herz} beats fast when I'm nervous.
sentences: This café has so much {heart}!
I love this place with all my {heart}.

definition: Eyes (plural). The singular is 'das Auge'.
examples: Close your {Augen} and make a wish!
sentences: Close your {eyes} and smell this coffee!
My {eyes} are tired from reading all day.

definition: Book. Related to English 'book' — same Germanic roots.
examples: Can you pass me that {Buch} on the shelf?
sentences: I found this great {book} on the shelf!
Can I read my {book} in the reading room?

definition: Flower. Related to English 'bloom'!
examples: He gave her a {rot} {Blume} for her birthday.
sentences: That {flower} on the table smells wonderful!
I love the {flower} arrangements in your café.

definition: Tree. 'Weihnachtsbaum' is a Christmas tree!
sentences: The {tree} in the garden gives such nice shade!
I love sitting under that {tree} on the patio.

definition: Sky or heaven. 'Himmelblau' means sky-blue.
examples: Look at the stars in the {Himmel} tonight.
sentences: The {sky} looks amazing from the garden!
What a clear {sky} — perfect patio weather!

definition: Sea or ocean. Germans love vacationing at the Meer!
examples: I can hear the {Meer} from my window.
sentences: I wish this café was by the {sea}!
This painting of the {sea} on the wall is lovely.

definition: Earth — the planet or the ground beneath your feet.
sentences: The plants need more {earth} in their pots.
I love the smell of fresh {earth} in the garden.
